negative_findings.description: Search-engine queries in both uk and en for Ukrainian bank vacancies explicitly naming 'SmartVista' (BPC) returned no live vacancy pages, only generic djinni/board landing pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: SmartVista appears as a platform name in vendor/reference material but was not surfaced in any indexed Ukrainian vacancy text during this scouting pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Absence in search indexes is not absence in the market — vacancy bodies on work.ua/robota.ua/djinni are often poorly indexed. On-site keyword search on each board is required before concluding BPC has no UA footprint.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated engineering/tech blog was found for monobank/Fintech Band or PrivatBank via uk-language search; results returned press coverage (ITC.ua, NV, Forbes.ua) and Wikipedia rather than a first-party engineering blog.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank-owned engineering blogs appear to be largely absent in Ukraine; technical disclosure happens instead through DOU articles, podcasts and conference talks.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The 'bank engineering blog' branch of this cell is thin; collection effort should be reallocated to DOU editorial/podcast content and vacancy texts, and to conference-talk listings, rather than to first-party blogs.

negative_findings.description: No vacancy or careers page was located for Ukrainian PSPs Fondy, Portmone, EasyPay or Concord-related acquirers in this pass; the PSP query returned only UPC.
negative_findings.result_summary: PSP-side hiring signal remains uncovered; only the bank and third-party-processor sides were mapped.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: PSP/acquirer stack signals (gateway, tokenisation, POS estate) are a distinct and commercially important layer that this pass did not reach.

negative_findings.description: No page was fetched or liveness-tested in this pass; all URLs come from search-result listings only.
negative_findings.result_summary: All candidate URLs are provided at stated confidence without any liveness claim.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must resolve every URL, especially bot-defended domains (LinkedIn, Indeed, djinni) where a 403 should be read as bot-defended-but-live rather than dead.

coverage_gaps.description: PSP/acquirer and payment-institution employers (Fondy, Portmone, EasyPay, iPay, Platon, LeoGaming and NBU-registered payment institutions) have no mapped career sources.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull the NBU register of payment institutions, map each entity's careers/Telegram/DOU presence, and add per-employer vacancy sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-name keyword hunting was done via general web search, which indexes vacancy bodies poorly; on-site search of each board was not performed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run on-site keyword searches (Way4, SmartVista, Б2, Is-Card, ISCB, SAP Banking, Temenos, Oracle Flexcube, Diasoft, NCR, Diebold, Wincor, Glory, FIS) directly inside work.ua, robota.ua, djinni.co and jobs.dou.ua and archive the result sets.

coverage_gaps.description: Vacancies expire and are deleted, so retrospective stack history cannot be reconstructed from live boards alone.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snapshot vacancy pages into the archive on each crawl and query the Wayback Machine for historical board/company pages to build a multi-year vendor-mention time series.

coverage_gaps.description: Engineering-community output beyond job boards — conference talks (DOU Day, Fwdays, iForum), YouTube tech talks and university/partner training programmes run by banks — was not scouted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add UA tech-conference agendas and bank-run academies as a separate source group; speaker abstracts routinely name production platforms.

coverage_gaps.description: The two highest-density sources (LinkedIn, and CV databases) are the most access- and privacy-constrained.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide a compliant access route before building collection: licensed LinkedIn access or analyst-manual review; for CVs, collect only anonymised stack signals and never personal identifiers.

brief: Ukraine's indirect vendor-stack signal is concentrated in four layers: mass job boards (work.ua, robota.ua) whose vacancy texts name core-banking and card platforms outright — АБС Б2 by CS Ltd, Is-Card, СЕП/ISO 20022 — plus ATM brands (NCR, Diebold, Wincor, Glory) in field-service roles; IT-community boards (djinni.co, jobs.dou.ua) covering the large in-house bank IT teams and the dominant third-party processor UPC; first-party career portals for banks that run their own ATS (PrivatBank, PUMB, NBU) and for small banks invisible elsewhere; and DOU editorial, which supplies the annual bank-IT-headcount ranking that prioritises every other source. First-party bank engineering blogs are effectively absent in this market — technical disclosure flows through DOU articles/podcasts and vacancy texts instead, so collection effort belongs there. The main uncovered layer is the PSP/acquirer side, and the main methodological weakness is that vacancy bodies index poorly in general search, so on-site keyword search per board plus snapshot archiving is required to turn these sources into a usable time series.
